I'm a 43-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with 3 mu of land. Been farming since I was 23 — that's 20 years. I grow stevia on all 3 mu. Switched from wheat-maize about 6 years ago because on such a small plot, grain barely covers costs after you buy seed, fertilizer, and pay for pumping water. My cousin in the western part of the county told me stevia leaves sell to the processing plant for decent money, so I tried it and it worked out okay.

This year I'll do more or less the same as last year. I learned the hard way not to change too much. One year I thought more fertilizer would mean more leaves, but they grew too big and watery and the buyer docked my price. Now I stick to what I know.

**Planting:** Late April, around the 25th, when the soil has warmed up. I buy seedlings from the nursery in town — costs me about 100 yuan per mu. Me and my wife transplant by hand. Takes us about 3 days for the whole plot. Used to be faster when my son lived at home, but he works in a factory in Handan now.

**Fertilizer:** I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — the 15-15-15 kind, about 50 jin (25 kg). Then in mid-June when the plants start growing fast, I topdress with another 20 jin (10 kg) of urea per mu. The extension guy told me stevia doesn't need heavy feeding, and I've found that's about right. Total fertilizer cost around 170 yuan per mu.

**Irrigation:** I'll water right after transplanting so the seedlings take root. Then probably twice more in summer when the rain doesn't come — mid-July and mid-August. Three times total. The well pump runs on electricity, costs about 20 yuan each time per mu. Flood irrigation, same as everyone around here.

**Pesticides:** I spray herbicide once after transplanting to keep weeds down, about 40 yuan per mu. For insects, I watch for aphids. If they show up in August, I'll spray once. If not, I save the money. Budget about 60 yuan per mu for chemicals total.

**Tillage:** I hire my neighbor's rotary tiller in early April when the field dries out — 30 yuan per mu. I used to till by hand but my back can't take it anymore.

**Labor:** Family does almost everything. Me and my wife put in about 20-25 days total across the season. For harvest in late September, if the crop looks heavy, I might hire one person for 2 days to help cut and carry. That's 150 yuan per day. My son usually comes home that weekend to help too.

**Yield and money:** Last year I got about 200 kg of dried leaves per mu. This year I'm hoping for 220-230 kg if the summer rain cooperates. Buyer pays about 8 yuan per kg, so I figure around 5,500 yuan gross. After all costs — seed, fertilizer, chemicals, pumping, tillage, and hired help — that's about 1,500 yuan out. I should clear around 4,000 yuan. Not getting rich, but it's steady, and with my son's factory wages we get by.
